clue.text: Latin poet sustaining warlike aspect

parts.note: Martial was the Roman epigrammatist of the first century AD
sustaining a weight is bearing it

explanation.surface: A Roman poet is shown keeping up a fierce, soldierly look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin poet' suggests Virgil or Ovid, but the poet here doubles as the adjective for war.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldierly carriage or demeanour is a military posture, the look of someone ready for battle.

clue.text: Mum's wise to knead the joint!

parts.note: mum is MA, and the 's adds an S
a wise person is a sage, and sage also means wise

explanation.surface: A mother with good sense is told to work on an aching joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading muscles and joints with the hands is exactly what a masseur does.

clue.text: Isaac's wife booked by Daphne du Maurier

explanation.surface: A biblical wife seems to have been reserved by a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked by' means written as a book by: du Maurier's 1938 novel bears the name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch Isaac marries this woman, and the same name titles du Maurier's famous gothic novel.

clue.text: Theories put aside in disarray

indicators.note: something in disarray is jumbled, so the letters of aside are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Theories are abandoned because they have fallen into a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put aside' reads as one phrase meaning discarded; 'put' is only a link and 'aside' is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are notions or concepts, the plural of a thought someone has formed.

clue.text: Comparatively tardy partner directed sideways

parts.note: the comparative of late, tardy, is later
an ally is a partner in a cause

explanation.surface: A partner who arrives later than expected is sent off to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving to the side rather than forwards is moving in a sideways direction.

clue.text: See 1
Ali Baba's ilk includes the aromatic herb man

indicators.note: the phrase Ali Baba's ilk includes the answer within its run of letters

explanation.surface: Ali Baba and his sort are said to contain a fragrant herbalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'BabA'S ILk'. The definition does double service as a herb and a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic plant used in pesto shares its name with a common boy's name.

clue.text: Band score transposed by runaway

indicators.note: music transposed is moved to another key; here the letters of band score are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A runaway musician rewrites the band's music in a different key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transposed' sounds musical beside 'score', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who absconds flees secretly, a fugitive or escapee.

clue.text: One does tend to hang about outside the pub

definitions.text: One does tend to hang about outside the pub

parts.words: One does tend to hang about outside the pub
parts.note: reads like a loiterer by a bar, but describes the painted board hanging over a tavern door

explanation.surface: Someone who always loiters outside the local.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a drinker loafing about; 'hang' is literal, a board hung outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern's painted board hangs on a bracket outside, showing its name.

clue.text: Lady Gee is upset by such an amorous look

indicators.note: being upset means disturbed, so the letters of Lady Gee are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A titled lady is offended by a flirtatious glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A flirtatious, inviting glance is an idiom for a come-hither look.

clue.text: Topic owing obedience to political rule

explanation.surface: A theme concerning loyalty to the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a matter under discussion, and a people bound to a ruler's authority are subservient to that crown.

clue.text: Indian money's returned to us retrospectively in her name

indicators.note: looking backwards in time, so the word us is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so this piece is written in reverse

parts.note: the anna was an old Indian coin, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Some Indian cash comes back to us, looked at in hindsight, under a woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The anna was a sixteenth of a rupee. 'Retrospectively' and 'returned' each turn their own piece, and the answer takes 'us' first.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in the biblical story of the elders.

clue.text: Lancaster reorganised as pertaining to our forebears

indicators.note: something reorganised is put into a new arrangement, as the letters of Lancaster are

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern English city is reshaped, in keeping with our ancestors.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCASTER is the county town of Lancashire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: What is inherited from forefathers belongs to one's lineage.

clue.text: Sheepish half dozen in one container .

indicators.note: the word one acts as a container, holding the other piece inside it

parts.note: taken as written
six, VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Feeling bashful about six eggs packed into a single box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like shy, but it means literally of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to sheep, as bovine does to cattle.

clue.text: … and after the Spanish, the African beast

indicators.note: after places the word and behind the Spanish article

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, an animal follows a Spanish article.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry the sense on from 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest antelope, a native of southern and eastern Africa.

clue.text: Good advice to country lovers in Kansas

explanation.surface: Sound counsel for rustic sweethearts in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'dodge city', the phrase tells country-lovers to avoid towns; it is also the Wild West town.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoiding urban life suits those who love rural areas, and the cattle town is in the Midwest state.

clue.text: Goodnight waltz at the cobbler's ball?

explanation.surface: The final waltz of the evening at a shoemaker's dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler shapes shoes on a last, so his ball would be a dance of lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing number at a ball is the final turn on the floor, and a last is the cobbler's shoe-form.

clue.text: Team directors in the dining room

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: A squad and its managers meeting over dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a piece of furniture found in the dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: A long cabinet for plates and dishes stands against a wall where meals are taken.

clue.text: Classical nymph with a mouth full of venom

explanation.surface: A mythological nymph with poison in her mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the king cobra, a venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a tree nymph lives and dies with her tree, and the same name is given to the king cobra.

clue.text: Hard-wearing material from the Netherlands

explanation.surface: Durable cloth imported from the Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough linen fabric for blinds bears the name of the Dutch provinces, used for the whole country.

clue.text: Baleful result of complicated life in a short raincoat

indicators.note: in places the jumbled piece inside the raincoat

parts.note: MAC is the shortened form of mackintosh, a raincoat

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters of life are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy outcome of a muddled life spent in a cheap raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: ELIF (life mixed by 'complicated') goes inside MAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleful and the other word both mean causing harm or evil.

clue.text: Anchorages for the motorist

explanation.surface: Places to moor ships, and something for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltered water off a coast where ships ride at anchor is called this, and drivers travel on highways.

clue.text: Can I become likeable?

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they can grow pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words, AM I ABLE says 'Can I'; 'become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Can I means am I able, and likeable means friendly and pleasant.

clue.text: Good to look at varied lights? Say why

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters of lights are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word that follows as spoken

parts.note: the word why is spoken as the letter Y

explanation.surface: A display of changing lights is pleasant to look at, but someone asks the reason.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGHTL is the anagram of LIGHTS; 'Say' turns 'why' into Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasing to the eye means attractive, the opposite of unsightly.

clue.text: Ailing in the French textile city

indicators.note: in places the sickly word inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
someone ailing is ill

explanation.surface: Someone falls sick in a French manufacturing town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the French' reads as 'in France'; LE is the article that holds ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern French city was historically a major cloth-making centre.

clue.text: Repulsive epithet for re-polishing

explanation.surface: A disgusting label for the act of polishing again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repulsive' here means repelling; split as re-buffing, the word describes polishing a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving someone away means rejecting them, and to buff is to polish, so re-buffing is polishing again.

clue.text: Paradoxical though it may sound, it is brought down

definitions.text: Paradoxical though it may sound, it is brought down

parts.words: Paradoxical though it may sound, it is brought down
parts.note: the word for demolished is pronounced like the word for lifted up, hence the paradox

explanation.surface: Something sounds as if it went up, yet it fell.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like 'raised' but means razed, levelled to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolished or levelled to the ground, an old spelling of razed.

clue.text: Loud left-winger with a girl's name

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a socialist or communist is a red

explanation.surface: A noisy socialist goes by a female name.
explanation.walkthrough: F stands for forte in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, short for Winifred or Alfreda.

clue.text: Romances that could be pub-lie business

explanation.surface: Love affairs that might become matters for the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Romances are love liaisons, and public business is the matters of state.

clue.text: Not much Scotch and a tiny bite-there's no end to it

parts.note: wee is Scots for tiny

indicators.note: the bite has no end, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a bite of food, written out

explanation.surface: A small Scottish nibble that seems never to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, but it means in Scots speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots phrase means a small amount, a little.

clue.text: Shy deed, but lured into trap

indicators.note: in places the bashful word inside the act

parts.note: a deed is an act, written out
shy means coy

explanation.surface: A truly bashful creature was nevertheless enticed into a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'indeed' must be split as 'in deed' for the container to work; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoy draws birds into a trap, so to have been lured is to have been enticed.

clue.text: Where the head of the chapter may normally be found

definitions.text: Where the head of the chapter may normally be found

parts.words: Where the head of the chapter may normally be found
parts.note: the head of a cathedral chapter is its dean, and this is his official house

explanation.surface: Where a book's chapter title usually sits.
explanation.walkthrough: The chapter is a cathedral's clergy, not a section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The residence of the cleric who heads a cathedral's clergy.
